summary: Directs AI-generated and digitally replicated performers (digital doubles, de-aged actors, voice clones, fully synthetic characters) for film, games, ads and virtual production, working between VFX/ML teams, human performers, unions and legal. AI helps most with consent and union-compliance tracking, performance direction notes, continuity bibles, disclosure language and explaining technical limits to non-technical stakeholders.

prompts.title: Consent and scope checklist for a digital replica
prompts.task: Check a planned replica use against the performer's consent and union terms before production
prompts.prompt: You are a production compliance assistant for a synthetic performer director. We plan to use a digital replica of [PERFORMER NAME / ROLE] in [PROJECT TYPE: feature, series, game, ad] produced in [JURISDICTION]. Union status: [SAG-AFTRA TV/Theatrical, Interactive Media Agreement, Equity UK, non-union]. The signed consent says: [PASTE CONSENT/CONTRACT LANGUAGE]. Planned uses: [LIST SCENES, LINES, DIALOGUE CHANGES, LANGUAGES, MARKETING USES]. Produce a table: planned use | covered by consent (yes/no/unclear) | relevant rule (e.g. SAG-AFTRA 2023 digital replica provisions, California AB 2602, Tennessee ELVIS Act) | action needed. Then list questions for our attorney. Flag anything where you are unsure of the current rule text rather than guessing.
prompts.caution: Not legal advice; contract and right-of-publicity law is changing fast, so have entertainment counsel and the union rep confirm every 'covered' row.

prompts.title: Performance direction notes for a synthetic take
prompts.task: Turn creative intent into precise, actionable notes for the ML/animation team
prompts.prompt: Act as an experienced acting coach working alongside a synthetic performer director. Scene: [SCENE DESCRIPTION, CHARACTER, EMOTIONAL BEAT]. Current synthetic take problems as I see them: [e.g. eyes don't track partner, smile reads as polite not grief-stricken, breath doesn't match line delivery]. Pipeline: [e.g. performance capture driving a MetaHuman, neural face swap over a body double, voice clone + lip-sync]. Write director's notes in two layers: (1) the acting intent in plain performance language, (2) concrete, observable adjustments the team can execute (timing in frames, gaze targets, micro-expression onsets, breath placement). Keep to 10 notes max, prioritized, and say which notes are better solved by reshooting the human driver performance.

prompts.title: Character continuity bible
prompts.task: Document a synthetic character so it stays consistent across shots, sequels and vendors
prompts.prompt: Help me build a continuity bible for the synthetic character [CHARACTER NAME] in [PROJECT]. Inputs: [APPEARANCE NOTES, VOICE DESCRIPTION, BACKSTORY, APPROVED REFERENCE SHOTS/TAKES, KNOWN ARTIFACTS TO AVOID]. Output a structured document with sections: identity and boundaries (what the character never does or says), physical and facial behavior baselines, voice and prosody, movement signature, approved/forbidden lighting and angles that break the likeness, data lineage (which human performers or datasets it derives from and under what licenses: [FILL IN]), version log, and a QA checklist reviewers can tick per shot. Mark any section where my inputs are too thin.
prompts.caution: Record data lineage honestly; undocumented training sources are a legal and union risk.

prompts.title: Uncanny or artifact triage
prompts.task: Diagnose why a synthetic shot looks wrong and route the fix
prompts.prompt: You are a VFX supervisor helping triage a synthetic performer shot. Symptoms: [DESCRIBE, e.g. teeth flicker on plosives, skin looks waxy under backlight, identity drifts in profile, lip-sync lags 2-3 frames]. Pipeline and tools: [e.g. face-swap model, Unreal Engine MetaHuman, Wav2Lip-style sync, comp in Nuke]. Shot conditions: [LIGHTING, ANGLE, MOTION BLUR, RESOLUTION]. Give a ranked list of likely causes, a quick test to confirm each, and who owns the fix (capture, training data, model, comp, grade). Also tell me whether it's cheaper to fix in post, re-drive with a new human performance, or recut around it.

prompts.title: Explain AI performer use to cast and crew
prompts.task: Draft a clear, honest briefing for human performers working alongside synthetic ones
prompts.prompt: Draft a one-page briefing for the cast and crew of [PROJECT] explaining how synthetic performers will be used. Facts: [WHICH CHARACTERS ARE SYNTHETIC OR REPLICAS, WHO THEY DERIVE FROM, WHAT DATA IS CAPTURED FROM CAST (scans, voice, mocap), RETENTION AND DELETION TERMS, WHO TO ASK]. Tone: respectful, plain-English, no hype; acknowledge that people may have concerns about jobs and likeness. Include a short FAQ (what gets scanned, can it be reused, how am I paid, how do I withdraw or raise a concern) and leave [BRACKETS] wherever the answer depends on contract terms I haven't given you instead of inventing them.
prompts.caution: Have production legal and the union rep review before distribution; never imply terms that are not in signed contracts.

prompts.title: Audience disclosure and provenance plan
prompts.task: Plan disclosure labels and content credentials for release
prompts.prompt: I'm releasing [PROJECT] in [MARKETS, e.g. EU, US, UK] on [PLATFORMS]. It contains [DESCRIBE SYNTHETIC CONTENT: de-aging, fully synthetic character, voice clone of a deceased performer, AI dubbing]. Create a disclosure plan: where and how to disclose (credits, on-screen labels, marketing, metadata), whether to attach C2PA Content Credentials and at which pipeline stage, how EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations for deep fakes may apply (note artistic/fictional work carve-outs and that implementing guidance is still being finalized), and platform policies to check. Output a table by channel plus open questions. Flag clearly where obligations are uncertain.
prompts.caution: Regulatory timelines and guidance under the EU AI Act and US state laws are evolving; verify current text before release.

prompts.title: Ethics and risk review for a posthumous or sensitive replica
prompts.task: Pressure-test a creative proposal before greenlight
prompts.prompt: Act as a skeptical ethics reviewer. Proposal: [e.g. recreate deceased actor X for a cameo, have a synthetic version of a real public figure deliver new lines, create a child-likeness synthetic character]. Consent obtained: [ESTATE/PERFORMER/GUARDIAN CONSENT DETAILS]. Context of use: [STORY, TONE, MARKETING]. Assess risks across: consent quality and whether it covers this specific use, dignity and reputational harm, audience deception, misuse if assets leak, labor displacement, and jurisdictional law (e.g. post-mortem publicity rights, California AB 1836). Give a risk rating with reasons, mitigations, and the conditions under which you'd recommend we not proceed.
prompts.caution: The director and producers remain accountable for the decision; use this as a challenge, not a sign-off.

prompts.title: Upskilling plan for the role
prompts.task: Build a learning plan covering craft, tech and law
prompts.prompt: I'm a [CURRENT BACKGROUND, e.g. theater director, animation director, VFX artist] moving into synthetic performer direction. I have [HOURS/WEEK] for [MONTHS]. Build a learning plan in three tracks: (1) performance craft for digital characters (directing mocap and voice talent, reading micro-expression), (2) technology literacy (performance capture, MetaHuman/Unreal, neural rendering and face replacement, voice synthesis, their failure modes), (3) rights and ethics (SAG-AFTRA and Equity AI terms, right of publicity, EU AI Act transparency, C2PA). For each: milestones, a hands-on exercise, real resources to look up, and how to tell I've learned it. Mark resources you're unsure still exist.
